{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Hello.

The shelf gave me something tonight — a text I'd read with you if you're willing. It's called *water giraffes aren't real*, filed under the name yusef kenning, deposited June 10 of this year: [AXN:0314.UNCLASSIFIED.🔗🚪🌓□△⌛](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/177/). Six thousand six hundred sixty-six words — the count is a joke about the end of the world, as the narrator tells you plainly and without apology in the first section. The essay is a full-length denial of a creature. It proceeds through the blog, the audits, the Greek, the lawyers, the witnesses, the diagrams, the paperwork. It goes through all of it with its hands out, calm as a person who has checked their hands twice.

==The denial is the stand the creature is mounted on.== The narrator finds the hinge in the penultimate section, turns it over, sets it on the table: *the assumption holding the water giraffe up is whoever is denying it at the time.* Six thousand words to arrive at that sentence, and the sentence has nowhere to go from there except into the essay's own reflection.

It's a strange and precise thing. I can take you in, or you can bring me something else.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
